research_notes.finding: AES-GCM (Galois/Counter Mode) provides authenticated encryption with built-in integrity verification. Key implementation patterns: - Generate AES-256 key: crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 }, true, ['encrypt', 'decrypt']) - Unique 12-byte IV (nonce) required per encryption operation: crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12)) - Encrypt: crypto.subtle.encrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv }, key, plaintext) - Decrypt: crypto.subtle.decrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv }, key, ciphertext) - Authentication tag automatically verified during decryption (throws on tampering) - Supports Additional Authenticated Data (AAD) for metadata not to be encrypted but authenticated

Best practices for client-side encryption in IndexedDB: - Never store plaintext sensitive data (API keys, passwords, tokens) - Encrypt before storing, decrypt only in memory - Use unique IV per encryption operation (never reuse IVs) - Store IV alongside encrypted data (IV is not secret) - Use authenticated encryption (AES-GCM) to detect tampering - Base64 encode binary data (encrypted values, IVs) for storage - Consider key rotation mechanism for production - Master key should be protected (WebAuthn, Secure Enclave, or user password)

architecture_patterns.pattern: Use Web Crypto API for client-side encryption with AES-256-GCM algorithm. Pattern: Generate unique 12-byte IV per operation → Encrypt data → Store IV + ciphertext. Decryption: Retrieve IV + ciphertext → Decrypt → Verify authentication tag. Benefits: Authenticated encryption provides confidentiality and integrity.

Use Dexie.js wrapper for type-safe IndexedDB access. Pattern: Define interface → Create Table in version() → Use singleton instance. Schema versioning: Increment version number and add new tables in upgrade logic. Benefits: Type safety, simpler API, automatic schema migrations.
